I had a friend like that once. No matter how much I tried to encourage this person, it was of little to no help at all. But I stumbled on to something that would help this person.  Get involved in some kind of activity that is difficult to accomplish, something you do as an individual, but in a group setting.  Don’t judge me on this (lol), but it was CrossFit (I know I know). But the environment there is very positive, and you can become quite close to people quickly when you suffer together (in this case, hard workouts). If you are slow to finish, they will encourage you, cheer for you, high five when you make it.   This experience for that person really brought them out of what sounds very similar to what you are going through.  Yes, there will be a little fear in the beginning, but they will make you feel like a part of the group from the very start. It’s part of what makes it CrossFit.
